A1_re_derived_at_head.claim_checked: the engine's own clock brackets the writer invocation, independent of writer self-reporting, and both writer shapes (light/heavy) funnel through the same timed call

timing_bracket.code: substep_started = time.monotonic(); result = writer.run_substep(ctx, step); substep_elapsed = time.monotonic() - substep_started
timing_bracket.note: monotonic() brackets ONLY writer.run_substep, not the SAVEPOINT/RELEASE either side of it, and is summed across every executed substep into duration_seconds, returned to the caller. A skipped (already-resumed) substep is never timed and contributes 0.

both_shapes_funnel_through_the_same_call.finding: WriterBase.plan_substeps defaults to `[SubStep(key=self.asset_id, ...)]` (one substep) and run_substep defaults to `return self.run(ctx)`. A light writer therefore executes its run() body INSIDE _drive_substeps' single call to run_substep — the identical timed call site as a heavy writer's real substep loop. There is no separate, untimed code path for light writers.

writer_census_by_shape.method: AST scan of every class decorated with a bare @register(...) call across platform/python-sidecar, excluding test/__tests__ directories and test_*.py files; classified 'heavy' if the class overrides plan_substeps or run_substep, else 'light' if it overrides run, else 'neither'
writer_census_by_shape.reconciliation: NOT reconciled to an exact match — a small (2-3 writer) discrepancy against the prior session's census, most likely a difference in enumeration script (e.g. which directories/aliases were counted as 'production'), not a difference in the underlying claim. The qualitative claim — that both shapes dispatch through the identical time.monotonic()-bracketed call in _drive_substeps — is verified directly from source in this session independent of the exact count, and does not depend on which of the two counts is more precise.

cascade_shape.verdict: This is NOT a single root cause reducible to one asset — it is a fan-out cascade. 557 of 1236 rows name exactly one immediate upstream blocker; the remaining 679 name two or more, because DAG-central hub assets (bo_laksana, ph_nimitta, ka_sangam, bo_sangati, bo_bimba, bo_karanajala) sit at points where multiple sibling dependencies fail together in the same run.

root_cause_characterization.method: sampled the top-named upstream assets' OWN build_run_assets rows to see what actually failed them (root failure vs. themselves being blocked)
root_cause_characterization.finding: The top hub assets' own failures are dominated by the SAME infra-class families already characterized elsewhere in this record: bo_laksana's own error/aborted rows are mostly 'orphaned_by_crash' (11), 'guardian_cleanup' (4), 'worker_crash' (2), plus a smaller number of nested BLOCKED-on-ga_* cascades and one DEP-ASSERT. ka_sangam shows the same pattern (orphaned_by_crash 7, guardian_cleanup 5, worker_crash 3, nested BLOCKED-on-bo_laksana 15) plus ONE genuine causal bug: 'RuntimeError: ka_sangam: could not resolve Moon nakshatra for chart 1c826d5a...' (3 records).
root_cause_characterization.conclusion: One cause, N blocked — but the 'one cause' is not a single literal, it is a small, recurring set of infra-class interruptions (orchestrator crash / manual guardian cleanup / worker crash) landing repeatedly on a handful of DAG-central hub assets (bo_laksana, ph_nimitta, ka_sangam foremost), each of which then fans out to hundreds of downstream BLOCKED records through ordinary cascade propagation. This matches this session's own git history: 'L2 cycle #81 final: BO_LAKSANA FROZEN — campaign hinge cleared' (commit 0cb89e971, this same repo, this same week) independently corroborates bo_laksana as a long-standing, named chronic blocker in this exact campaign, not a diagnostic artifact of this report.

gate_judgement.verdict: GATE PASS — with the production-verification boundary stated plainly and not overstated.
reasoning: A2: 0 residual empty-error-capable failed-state paths at HEAD, verified directly from source across BOTH TypeScript and Python (the task's explicit ask, since the original A2 measurement scoped only TS). This is a code-level guarantee, fully re-derivable and independent of any deploy.

The three production before-figures this gate was asked to hold as controls are, for three of their four defining sub-populations (empty-error, frozen-manifest, rows_per_second-null), reproduced EXACTLY. The fourth (raw error/aborted denominator) drifted for reasons independently investigated and ruled unrelated to Phase A.
Nothing in the record shows Phase A's commits worsening anything — the last real build predates all four commits by a week, and no new error family appeared.

What remains genuinely unverifiable until deploy: whether the production asset_throughput.rows_per_second actually populates on a real build (blocked on the deliberately-unapplied migration 1094), and whether A3's narrowed-blast-radius behavior holds on a REAL registry divergence rather than the counterfactual replay against the real d4a6dae2 manifest and a synthetic unit reconstruction. Both are honestly labelled 'unverifiable in production until deploy' rather than papered over.
gate_judgement.what_would_upgrade_this_to_a_stronger_pa: A single real build run through the corrected engine after migration 1094 is applied — not manufactured to flatten a metric, but the first ordinary build that happens to occur post-deploy — would convert A1's production figure from NULL to a real measurement and would let A3's narrowing be observed on a genuine divergence rather than only proven counterfactually and at the unit level.
gate_judgement.what_would_fail_this_gate_and_did_not_ha: Any of: a residual TS or Python path still capable of writing empty error text (none found); the validator still raising on first mismatch (it does not); dependents failing outright instead of blocking (they block); evidence that Phase A's commits caused new failures or new empty-error records (none found).
